steps.title: Sharpen tungsten needle
steps.instruction: Cut 3 cm off a 0.25 mm tungsten wire, mount it in a metal needle holder, connect the holder’s metal handle to the (+) terminal of a transformer with a crocodile clip and the carbon plate cathode to the (–) terminal, place the carbon electrode in a glass chamber containing 100 ml of 5 M NaOH, switch on the transformer and set the output voltage to 6 V; hold the needle vertically and dip it repeatedly into and out of the NaOH solution moving slowly and steadily until the desired tip is formed (current gauge reads 0–1 A); the process takes ~2.5 min to reduce the tip diameter from 0.25 mm to 0.02 mm.

steps.title: Prepare insect‑pin instrument
steps.instruction: Take a clean glass Pasteur pipette, bend its thin side in the middle with a Bunsen burner to create a 45° angle, then close the hole of the thin side by heating the tip in the hottest part of the flame while rotating it until the opening is about three‑quarters closed; insert a 0.10 mm stainless‑steel insect pin (sharp side outward) into the hole with forceps, and gently re‑heat the weakest part of the flame until the hole is fully sealed and the pin is secured, avoiding overheating the pin.

steps.title: Make 1.5 % agarose layer
steps.instruction: Weigh 1.5 g agarose and melt it in 100 ml E3 embryo medium in a 250 ml glass bottle using a microwave; pour approximately 20 ml of the molten 1.5 % agarose into a Ø 90 mm petri dish to form a thin layer and allow it to solidify.

steps.title: Prepare 1:10,000 tricaine
steps.instruction: Dilute tricaine stock to a 1:10,000 working solution in E3 embryo medium (see recipe) and pour 30 ml of this solution into a Ø 90 mm petri dish.

steps.title: Anesthetize individual larva
steps.instruction: Transfer a single zebrafish larva (3–7 days post‑fertilization) into the 1:10,000 tricaine solution and wait until the larva is fully anesthetized.

steps.title: Perform notochord needle injury
steps.instruction: Place the anesthetized larva on its side on the solidified agarose‑coated petri dish so the lateral side is accessible; remove excess liquid so surface tension holds the larva in place; under a stereomicroscope, gently insert the sharpened tungsten tip vertically into the notochord at the level of the yolk‑sac end and then withdraw the needle.

steps.title: Recover injured larvae
steps.instruction: Transfer the injured larva to a petri dish containing fresh E3 medium, keep the dish at 28.5 °C for recovery and further growth, and maintain age‑matched uninjured larvae as non‑injured controls.

steps.title: Prepare 5 mg ml⁻¹ nystatin stock
steps.instruction: Dissolve 5 mg of nystatin in DMSO to obtain a 5 mg ml⁻¹ (5.4 mM) stock solution immediately before use.

steps.title: Dilute nystatin to 20 µM
steps.instruction: Add the appropriate volume of the 5 mg ml⁻¹ nystatin stock to E3 embryo medium to achieve a final concentration of 20 µM; add this solution to dechorionated 48 hpf embryos placed in a 6‑well plate.

steps.title: Add DMSO control
steps.instruction: Add 0.4 % (v/v) DMSO to control embryos in parallel with the nystatin treatment.

steps.title: Incubate embryos
steps.instruction: Incubate both nystatin‑treated and DMSO‑control embryos at 28.5 °C for up to 48 h; lesions typically become visible after 24 h of nystatin exposure.

steps.title: Prepare embryos for imaging
steps.instruction: Anesthetize embryos in 1:10,000 tricaine, mount them sagittally in 1 % low‑melt agarose, and acquire bright‑field images with a light microscope or confocal images of the R2‑col2a1a:mCherry and wt1b:GFP reporters.

steps.title: Tail amputation
steps.instruction: After anesthetizing a larva as above, place it on its side on the solidified agarose layer, remove excess liquid, and amputate the tail with a sterile scalpel blade applying slight pressure; select the amputation site (e.g., before caudal vein or past caudal vein) to include notochord tissue for wt1b:GFP induction.

steps.title: Recover amputated larvae
steps.instruction: Transfer the amputated larvae to a petri dish containing fresh E3 medium, keep at 28.5 °C, and keep uninjured age‑matched larvae as controls.

steps.title: Prepare E3 embryo medium (60×)
steps.instruction: Dissolve 17.4 g NaCl, 0.8 g KCl, 2.9 g CaCl₂·2H₂O, and 4.89 g MgCl₂·6H₂O in 1 L deionized water to make a 60× stock solution.

steps.title: Prepare 1× Tricaine solution
steps.instruction: Dissolve 0.1 g Tricaine powder in 1 L of 1× E3 medium and adjust the pH to 7.0.

steps.title: Prepare 5 M NaOH
steps.instruction: Dissolve 200 g NaOH pellets in 1 L deionized water to obtain a 5 M NaOH solution.
